title: Raw Archive Manifest
description: The meta.json manifest inside a BarSpeed raw-data zip: one descriptor per set, naming the CSV files the zip holds for it and the facts a reader who opens only the CSVs needs to interpret them -- which way the lift moved, how the sensor was mounted, which sensor was analysed, where the prep window was. The analysis itself is in the zip's session.json (session-export.schema.json); where a key here and a key there state one fact they use the same words, and the flat keys here correspond to nested objects there. Every unknown is expressed by omitting the key: this document writes no null literals. VERSION LOG. meta.json carries no version key of its own -- adding one would change the bytes of every manifest -- so this log is tied to the app build that wrote the file, which meta.json states as `appVersion`. 1.0 (appVersion 0.2.0, issue #326): first publication, describing meta.json exactly as RawExporter writes it on the 0.2.0 release branch. Builds of that branch made before its version bump, and v0.1.59 itself, write the same shape stamped 0.1.59. Within 1.0 (#297, export 1.26, lane L1 of that branch): a set of kind hold or carry writes no startsWith, concentric or concentricSource; a build of the branch made before that change, and v0.1.59, wrote all three for it. Within 1.0 (#337, lane L8 of that branch): a set that ran no prep and whose work the app let begin writes workStartedAt_ms equal to its startedAt_ms -- the START SET tap, which bounds no set-up motion after it -- alone, with no prepStartedAt_ms, so workStartedAt_ms no longer requires prepStartedAt_ms, and the rollExcursionBasis rules key on prepStartedAt_ms (a stored prep window) rather than on workStartedAt_ms; a build of the branch made before that change, and v0.1.59, wrote no work start on such a set. Within 1.0 (#336, lane L8 of that branch): a guided set whose recorded reps differ from the number of rep marks its cadence guide called writes repsSource "corrected" rather than "metronome", retroactively on re-export wherever the set's marks are stored, and with no liveReps beside it; the guide's calls are that set's _reps.csv rows, and meta.json carries no guideReps, so a manifest-only reader counts those rows for the guide's figure. A guided set at the guide's own count, or one with no stored marks, is unchanged. A build of the branch made before that change, and v0.1.59, wrote "metronome" for it. Within 1.0 (#242, #287, export 1.26, lane L10 of that branch): `analysedFellBack` and `sensorsSilent` also cover an armed unit that delivered enough frames to analyse but whose stream spanned less of the set than its partner's, or that never moved while its partner did; the role is decided when a set is recorded and frozen with it, so the change is not retroactive. `sensorsSilent` names any refused unit only when its link was not delivering as the set ended. A build of the branch made before that change, and v0.1.59, set both only for an armed unit that delivered too few frames to analyse. Manifests written by earlier builds are not guaranteed to validate against it: v0.1.44 to v0.1.46 wrote a sensorsPlanned key this schema does not declare; v0.1.31 to v0.1.50 wrote rollExcursion_deg without rollExcursionBasis, as the range over the whole capture; builds up to v0.1.30 could write "sampleRate_hz": null, and builds before v0.1.38 could write it as 0.0. Read a manifest's appVersion before applying this schema to it. Every later change to what RawExporter writes into meta.json adds an entry here and moves this schema, its example and RawExporterTest's manifest pin in the same change; a key this schema does not declare fails validation, because every object here is closed.

epoch.description: The session's start instant, UTC, ISO-8601 with a Z. Every instant in this archive (the CSVs' timestamp_ms, prep_started_ms and work_started_ms columns and this manifest's *At_ms keys) is epoch milliseconds, not an offset from this. rr_ms in the HRM CSVs is an RR interval, not an instant.

utcOffsetMinutes.description: The device's UTC offset when the session was recorded, in minutes. Present with timeZoneId or not at all: absent on a session recorded before the app captured its zone. session.json carries the same fact as timeZone.utcOffsetMinutes.

timeZoneId.description: The device's zone id when the session was recorded (an IANA id such as Europe/London). Named timeZoneId rather than timeZone so one key never means a string here and an object in session.json.

appVersion.description: The versionName of the build that wrote this archive. Also the key this schema's version log is tied to.

sensorModel.description: The IMU model the app is built for. A constant string, not a reading from the sensor.

analysisFile.description: The zip entry that holds the full session analysis.

csvHeaderImu.description: The header row of every *_imu.csv and *_imu-<role>.csv in the zip, as written. Device-frame samples; one row per sample as it arrived.

csvHeaderHrm.description: The header row THIS build writes for every *_hrm.csv, *_rest_before_hrm.csv and *_rest_after_hrm.csv: `timestamp_ms,hr_bpm,rr_ms,contact` since export 1.26 (#82). Stored streams are copied into the zip verbatim, each with its own header line, so a stream recorded by an earlier build still has three columns, `timestamp_ms,hr_bpm,rr_ms`: read each file's own header for its width, never this key. `contact` is `1` where the strap reported skin contact, `0` where it reported none, and EMPTY where it said nothing; a three-column file means the same as empty on every row, never either reported value.

csvHeaderCues.description: The header row of every *_cues.csv: what the app spoke, and when.

csvHeaderReps.description: The header row of every *_reps.csv: the instants the live counter counted a rep.

csvHeaderPrep.description: The header row of every *_prep.csv: the prep window's two instants.

sets.description: One descriptor per recorded set, in the order the session recorded them.

set.description: 1-based position of this set in the session; also the NN of its set<NN>_ file names.

exercise.description: The exercise id the set was recorded under.

load_kg.description: The load as stored, in kilograms: on a body-weight set the sum including bodyWeight_kg.

load_lb.description: load_kg in pounds, rounded to 0.1. A conversion, not a second measurement.

bodyWeight_kg.description: The body-weight term inside load_kg. Absent on a set with none.

reps.description: The rep count recorded for the set; whose count it is, is repsSource. Absent on a timed set; a rep set's 0 is a count.

plannedLoad_kg.description: The load the plan prescribed, on load_kg's scale. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

workingLoad_kg.description: The load the set ran against, before any rest-screen correction. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

plannedReps.description: The rep count the plan prescribed. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

workingReps.description: The rep count the set ran against. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

plannedDuration_s.description: The hold or carry seconds the plan prescribed. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

workingDuration_s.description: The hold or carry seconds the set ran against. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

rest_s.description: The rest prescribed after this set, a minimum, in whole seconds. Never a measurement. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

restMeasured_s.description: The seconds from this set's stored rest instant to the next set's start. Absent on the last set of a session and where either instant is missing. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

tempoPrescribed.description: The tempo the set ran. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

plannedTempo.description: The tempo the plan prescribed. Same key and meaning as in session.json.

duration_s.description: A timed set's seconds. Absent on a rep set and on a set abandoned in its prep.

durationEndedBy.description: What decided duration_s. Absent where duration_s is absent, and on a set recorded before database v19, which stored no such word. The same words session.json publishes.

abandonedInPrep.description: The set never entered its work phase, so the zeros beside this are absences, not measurements. Omitted when false, and omission is not proof the work began: a set recorded before database v15 stores no answer and writes nothing here, as session.json's abandonedInPrep says.

side.description: The side the set was worked on, where one was recorded.

rpe.description: The lifter's effort rating, on rpeScale's scale.

rpeScale.description: Which question the rating answered. Absent where rpe is.

failed.description: The set was marked failed, by the lifter or by derivation. Absent otherwise.

failedByLifter.description: Whether the lifter said so (true) or the app derived it (false). Written only where failed is, and absent on a failed set recorded before database v15, which stored no author: there, omission says nobody knows, not that the app derived it.

analysisSchemaVersion.description: The session export contract current in the build that RECORDED this set and computed the analysis stored with it (#38), and nothing finer: an analysis change shipped without moving that contract is not distinguished by it. It carries the same value, under the same rule, as the set's `analysisSchemaVersion` in session.json. Absent on every set recorded before database v21, which stored no such fact: absent means not recorded, never the version of the build that wrote this archive.

limiter.description: The reason the lifter gave for stopping. Absent where none was asked or given.

limiterNote.description: The lifter's free-text note beside limiter. Written only where limiter is.

warmup.description: The set counts as a warm-up, by the plan's word or the lifter's mark. Absent otherwise.

warmupByLifter.description: The lifter stated this set's purpose themselves rather than leaving the plan's declaration to stand. Present with warmup ABSENT is a real statement: the lifter said the set was not a warm-up. Absent where the plan's word stands.

added.description: The lifter added this set; no plan prescribed it. Absent on a prescribed set.

voided.description: The lifter marked this set not performed. Absent otherwise.

voidReason.description: The lifter's reason for voided. Written only where voided is.

repsManual.description: reps is not an uncorrected sensor or segmenter count: the lifter's own taps, a correction to a count, or a guided set's cadence count. It never says a person counted the set; repsSource says whose count it is. Absent otherwise.

repsSource.description: Whose count reps is. The same words session.json publishes.

liveReps.description: What the live counter counted during the set. Absent where no live counter ran; 0 is a count.

plannedPrep_s.description: The prep the plan prescribed before this set, in whole seconds, or the app's default where none was declared. Absent where the row stored none.

prep_s.description: The prep that played before this set, in whole seconds; 0 is a prep in which nothing was spoken before the first stroke call. Absent on a set abandoned in its prep and where the row stored none.

startsWith.description: Which phase the set starts with. This and the next eight keys come from the set's stored geometry and are absent together on every set recorded before geometry was stored. This key, concentric and concentricSource -- the stroke words -- are written together or not at all, and only with the other six. The other six (plane, sensorOnStack, sensorInverted, travelRatio, kind, bodyweight) are written together, and without the stroke words on a set of kind hold or carry (#297, export 1.26): such a set has no stroke, so its stroke words would be an absence the resolver filled. session.json omits geometry.startsWith, geometry.concentric and their two geometry.source entries for such a set; GeometryExport.publishesStroke in the app's source makes both splits, and is not a key in either file.

concentricSource.description: Where concentric came from: session.json's geometry.source.concentric. `inferred` is in the vocabulary but is not written here, because this value is resolved with inference off.

plane.description: The plane of travel. Where sensorOnStack is true the stack travels vertically whatever this says, and that is the axis the analysis reads from the imu CSV, which carries all three.

sensorOnStack.description: The sensor rode a weight stack rather than the implement. Written true or false, never omitted, when geometry is.

sensorInverted.description: True when the sensor moved opposite to the load the lifter drove, the usual case with a sensor on a cable stack. The analysis flipped measured motion back into the lifter's frame. Not a statement about how the unit sits on its mount.

travelRatio.description: Lifter-side travel per unit of sensor travel: 1 for a direct mount, 2 for a 2:1 pulley. The same number and meaning as session.json's geometry.travelRatio. The analysis maps the sensor's motion into the lifter's frame by multiplying by this, negated where sensorInverted is true.

kind.description: The exercise kind the set was analysed as.

bodyweight.description: The exercise moves the lifter's body weight.

sensorsArmed.description: How many accelerometers the set was armed with. This key and sensorRolesExpected are written together, on a set that stored a sensor declaration, and are absent on an ordinary one-sensor set.

sensorsShortfall.description: Why the roster fell short of the roles a dual set needs. Absent when nothing was in the way.

sensorRolesExpected.description: The roles the set was armed to capture. Written even when empty.

analysedRole.description: The role whose stream every other figure in this descriptor describes.

analysedFellBack.description: The analysed role is not the role the set armed, because that unit could not stand for the set: it delivered too few frames to analyse, or, from export 1.26 (#242, #287), it delivered enough but its stream spanned less of the set than its partner's -- a late start or an early stop -- or it never moved while its partner did. No key here names the cause; the two roles' `samples` and imu CSVs show it, and session.json's `analysedFellBack` and `analysedRoleBasis` state the same fact in full. Absent otherwise.

analysedRoleBasis.description: Why that role was analysed. The same words session.json publishes.

sensorsSilent.description: Which armed units the analysis refused -- for too few frames to analyse, or, from export 1.26 (#242, #287), for a stream that spanned less of the set than its partner's or for a unit that never moved while its partner did -- and whose link was not delivering as the set ended, keyed by role, with what the app could see of each one's link at set end. A refused unit whose last frame landed inside the three seconds before the set ended is not named here, whatever it was refused for, so read `analysedFellBack` for whether the analysis moved. Written only when such a unit exists; session.json's `silent` is the same fact in the same words.

sensorsSoleSilent.description: The same word for a set whose single stream carries no role. Written only when that one link delivered too few frames to analyse and was not delivering as the set ended; session.json's `soleSilent` is the same fact.

startedAt_ms.description: The set's start instant, epoch milliseconds.

endedAt_ms.description: The set's end instant, epoch milliseconds.

prepStartedAt_ms.description: The prep window's start, epoch milliseconds, on the clock the IMU timestamp_ms column is stamped with. Written only where the set stored a prep window, and then always with workStartedAt_ms; a set that ran no prep has none.

workStartedAt_ms.description: Where the app let the set's work begin, epoch milliseconds. On a set that stored a prep window it is that window's end, and prepStartedAt_ms is written beside it. On a set that ran NO prep it is the START SET tap -- equal to startedAt_ms, the first instant of the capture -- and is written alone (#337). Where no prep ran, the app let the work begin at that tap: it adds no information a reader of startedAt_ms did not already have, and it does NOT bound set-up motion that follows the tap -- walking to the bar, plate handling, a set-up pull -- which on the 24 Sep 225 x 5 deadlift ran inside a 138 s capture. It is the app's lower bound on the work, not an observation of it; where the lifter actually began lifting on such a set is not recorded by anything, and this key alone cannot window set-up motion out. Absent where the instant is not known: a set that set out to run a prep and stored no window, a row written before v0.1.50 that cannot say whether its work began, or a set whose work never began.

sampleRate_hz.description: The mean rate the analysed stream's rows ARRIVED at -- (n-1) intervals over the span of their timestamps -- not the rate the sensor sampled at; the two are equal only if nothing was dropped. Absent where no rate can be stated, never zero.

rollExcursion_deg.description: How far the analysed sensor's unwrapped roll swept across the interval rollExcursionBasis names, in degrees, rounded to 0.1. Written with rollExcursionBasis or not at all.

rollExcursionBasis.description: Which interval rollExcursion_deg covers. workingWindow and fromWorkStart are written exactly when the set carries prepStartedAt_ms -- a stored prep window, whose end is the window's opening bound; toTerminalCue and wholeCapture exactly when it does not. A no-prep set's workStartedAt_ms is its capture's own start, so its roll is still reported over the capture and named so.

sensors.description: One entry per role-tagged IMU capture that arrived, each figure measured from its own stream. Absent on a set whose streams carry no role. A role in sensorRolesExpected with no entry here was armed and delivered nothing.

files.description: The zip entries that belong to this set, as named in the zip.

role.description: The role this capture was tagged with.

file.description: This capture's zip entry, one of the set's files.

samples.description: Rows in that file. Absent where the file will not decode.

sampleRate_hz.description: The mean arrival rate of this stream's rows, the set-level key's arithmetic over this stream alone. Absent where it cannot be stated.

rollExcursion_deg.description: This stream's roll excursion, as the set-level key.

rollExcursionBasis.description: Which interval this entry's rollExcursion_deg covers. The set-level rule holds here too, and the set descriptor enforces it: workingWindow or fromWorkStart exactly when the set carries prepStartedAt_ms, toTerminalCue or wholeCapture exactly when it does not, because every entry is windowed by the set's own stored prep window and terminal cue.
